narr: An early season low pressure system moved into southeastern California and cut off from the main steering flow. Leftover monsoon moisture from the subtropics combined with the stalled low pressure system and brought a 4 day period of severe weather and flash flooding.
ev: The USGS stream gauge on Big Chino Wash near Paulden (BCWA3) measured a 4.1 foot rise (877cfs) in about an hour and a half.
The county stream gauge at Mayer (54936 - Big Bug Creek @ SR 69) reported a 4.4 ft rise in 30 minutes, peaking at 1:55 pm.
A trained spotter reported a water rise greater than 4 feet in normally dry Big Bug Creek.
Public reported a rapid 4 foot water rise in Pine Creek at Tonto Natural Bridge State Park.
Public estimated 2 feet of water from Webber Creek flowing over the road entering Geronimo Estates.
Public reported water flowing over Fire Control Road in at least 8 spots west of Geronimo Estates.

Law enforcement reported flash flooding along Havasu Creek at Supai leading to trapped hikers. An upstream gauge (CCTA3) showed a rise from 4.05 ft to 5.95 ft from 12:15pm to 12:45pm MST, then another peak of 6.57 ft at 2:45pm MST. A downstream gauge (HNSA3) showed multiple peaks in streamflow from 800 to 1,200 cfs between 1:45pm and 6:00pm MST.
The Agua Fria below Ash Creek county river gauge (54897) measured a 3.75 foot rise between 5:00 pm and 5:50 pm MST with a peak streamflow of 3,354 cfs.
An mPING report was submitted of Sycamore Creek overflowing across Fire Control Road (Nf-64) near Pine.
